rulings.topic: Video walk: head down for the first ~3 s (gaze rule); lateral bob is a front/back-view quantity → per-facing bands; the packet stride re-cut head-up
rulings.ruling: Matt, verbatim: "1) THe head looks down for the first 3 seconds which is not correct for a purposeful character walking towards something in game. 2) The head will not show as much left-to-right bob as it is walking East. I suspect we will see more bob in N and S walks. But maybe I was off about the bob %.." (1) Gaze rule (Legolas W-7; the prompt asked for it): the clip holds the gaze only after ~3 s; the packet stride [53,87) = 2.2–3.6 s straddles the head-down window — which is also why the head tracker flagged frames 0–6 and W-2/W-3a read wide. Re-cut: K3p-xv-cut-04 = native [71,105) (2.96–4.38 s; DOWN at 71/88; before the ~4.5 s splice; the 4.3-s rule relaxed to 4.4 s with the splice check reported) → gates → packet B; packet A (as measured) kept. (2) Bands are PER FACING: vertical bob (W-1) in profile E/W; lateral sway (W-3) in front/back N/S — Legolas's lateral-suppression rule was written for front views; plate-13 front/rear rows exist uncommitted for N/S. On the bob %: the raw clip Matt passed bobs 2.06 %H vs the drawn target 4.93 — the target was off (R-50), not the eye.
rulings.consequence: Next clip prompts carry 'eyes on the horizon from the FIRST frame'; T3 adds a gaze/head-pitch check (W-7) and per-facing band rows; the N/S walk (a later clip) calibrates the lateral row. Cadence of the 12-frame cut remains an open rider.
